- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–72), model tends to lag; add 1–2% lag correction to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term downward trend; if sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 10–15 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model overfits short-term momentum; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.
